newsitem.title: UK: Spot copper treatment charges remain high.
newsitem.headline: Spot copper treatment charges remain high.

text.p: Treatment charges/refining charges (TC/RCs) for spot copper concentrates remain high, with recent business China-driven, industry specialists Bloomsbury Minerals Economics (BME) said.
In their latest monthly report BME said that the Chinese have been buying recently at T/Cs of $120/125 a tonne and R/Cs of 12.00/12.50 cents/lb. Other business has been around $130 and 13 cents.
In the blister market, the Chinese have been similarly active, taking spot at R/Cs of $100 a tonne or less.
Meanwhile, more details are emerging on annual deals in the concentrate market, Bloomsbury said.

It is understood that Freeport and LG Metals have concluded 1997 terms at $104.50/tonne and 10.5 cents/lb, with price participation (PP) of 10 percent above or below 90 cents/lb. The quotational period (QP) is the month after the month after arrival. This deal is believed to have been followed by Freeport and the Japanese smelters agreeing a combined TC/RC just under 27 cents/lb.
This equates to a separate T/C and R/C of $105/tonne and 10.5 cents/lb. The PP is said to be 10 percent above and below 90 cents/lb, with a QP of the third month after the month of arrival, BME said.
